standard.title: Features of local places
standard.description: the natural, managed and constructed features of local places, and their location
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFK03): Students identified features of familiar places and why some places are special. They used basic place vocabulary (near, far, natural, built).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify the natural, managed and constructed features of local places and describe their location.

nodes.label: Natural, managed and constructed features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can classify features of local places as natural (hills, rivers, vegetation, weather), managed (farms, parks, gardens) or constructed (roads, buildings), and give examples of each.
nodes.minimum_width: Classify at least six features across all three categories (natural, managed, constructed) with at least one example in each.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and classify a full range of natural, managed and constructed features in the local area; locate them on a provided map; explore Dreaming and Creation stories that identify natural features of place.
wider: Listen to and view First Nations Australian Dreaming and Creation stories that identify and explain the origin of natural features, discussing what these reveal about connections between people and place
Classify features of a contrasting place (e.g. a beach, a farm, a mountain) and compare with the local area
nodes.hinge_reason: The three-category classification is the analytical framework for this standard — without it, students cannot locate or discuss features coherently in subsequent nodes.

response_modes.reason: The natural/managed/constructed distinction is conceptually new at Year 1. Managed features are often confused with constructed ones — use sorting activities and decision trees to make the categories explicit.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Dreaming and Creation stories provide a qualitatively different lens on natural features — not just identifying them but understanding them as connected to cultural meaning and history.
success_criteria: Classifies at least two features as natural, two as managed and two as constructed
Gives a reason for each classification

nodes.label: Daily and seasonal weather
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the daily and seasonal weather of their local place using simple descriptive terms and compare it with weather in other places.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the local weather using at least four terms (rainy, hot, cold, windy, cloudy) and note one difference between local weather and weather somewhere else.
nodes.typical_width: Describe daily and seasonal weather patterns using a range of terms; compare weather across seasons; compare with weather of other known or familiar places.
wider: Record weather observations over a week or season and identify patterns
Compare weather of the local place with weather in a neighbouring region or a place connected to a family member's origin

response_modes.reason: Weather vocabulary requires repeated practice in context — daily weather recording builds fluency with the terms before comparative use.

success_criteria: Uses at least four weather terms accurately
Identifies one difference between weather in the local place and another place

nodes.label: Locating and describing features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain where features and places are located using direction and location terms, and locate them on a map.
nodes.minimum_width: Locate at least two features on a provided map and describe their position using at least two location terms (beside, near, forward, close to).
nodes.typical_width: Locate natural, managed and constructed features on a map of the local area; describe their position using a range of spatial terms (beside, forward, up, down, near, further, close to, before, after); explain directions to classmates.
wider: Create a simple map of the local area that shows the location and classification of natural, managed and constructed features
Describe a route between two features in the local area using direction terms in sequence

response_modes.reason: Locating features on a map integrates the three-category classification (what type of feature) with spatial reasoning (where it is) — the map is the integration task.

success_criteria: Locates at least two features on a provided map
Uses at least two location terms accurately to describe feature positions
